# Browser Validation

Use this to check user-visible behavior in the running ClassicForum app with the shared VS Code browser. Match the check to the change: cover affected journeys, not every route.

## 1. Establish Scope

1. If given a baseline commit, inspect `git diff --name-status <base>..HEAD` and `git log --oneline <base>..HEAD`.
2. Separate browser-visible routes and API flows from work a browser cannot verify, such as migrations, deployment scripts, or database transactions.
3. Read the relevant ticket or acceptance criteria. Browser checks do not prove server-side atomicity, authorization, migration safety, or test coverage.

## 2. Site Map and Common Workflows

ClassicForum is one Nuxt app with a shared navbar, tabbed page groups, and file-based routes under `app/pages/`. Use this map to find the normal UI path; check the current snapshot and enabled settings before assuming a control or tab is available.

- The brand/Home link opens `/feed`. Feed tabs include Search, Topics, Home, Posts, Links, Threads, Galleries, and Audio; settings may hide some tabs. `/feed` selects the remembered tab or an available default.
- Public routes include `/about`, `/contact`, `/topic/:topic`, and user/content details such as `/user/:id`, `/post/:id`, `/thread/:id`, `/link/:id`, and `/gallery/:id`.
- The signed-out navbar offers Login and Register. After sign-in, it offers Submit, Inbox, and the current profile. Moderator, Admin, and Developer links appear only for accounts with those roles; their page groups also enforce role checks.
- Authenticated Submit opens the tabbed editor. Available editor tabs depend on app settings and include Post, Link, Thread, Image, Audio, Video, and Poll.
- Other account and tool groups are `/profile` and `/settings/...`, `/inbox`, `/moderator/...`, `/admin/...`, and `/developer/...`. The profile route may redirect to the signed-in user's `/user/:id` page.
- Tabbed parent routes such as `/feed`, `/editor`, `/settings`, `/admin`, `/moderator`, and `/developer` can select a remembered or default child route. Verify the resulting URL instead of assuming the parent path remains active.

### Basic User Workflows

1. **Sign in or register:** from the signed-out navbar, choose Login or Register. After sign-in, Submit, Inbox, and the current profile appear. The profile link opens `/profile`, which redirects to `/user/:id`; on your own profile, choose Profile to reach `/settings/profile`. For another saved local account, use the profile link's context menu and choose `New Login`. Avoid removing a saved profile unless session invalidation is part of the test.
2. **Browse feeds:** choose the brand/Home link, then select an available feed tab. Open a result to inspect its detail page; follow its topic or author link to the corresponding profile. Profile and topic feeds provide New/Hot/Top sorting. Recheck enabled settings before treating a missing tab as a defect.
3. **Search content:** open Search, enter a word or phrase that appears in the item's title or content, then activate Search or press Enter. Expand filters to combine Type, Topic, Author, From, and To; changing these controls alone does not run the search. Text search and topic filtering are independent: searching a topic name will not find an item unless that text also matches the content. Confirm the URL query and result set after applying filters.
4. **Follow a topic or user:** open a topic from its chip or the Topics feed, or open an author's profile. Choose Follow and confirm it changes to Unfollow and the relationship count/state updates. Followed users and topics contribute to the authenticated Following feed. Use a disposable account for relationship tests that need isolation.
5. **Publish a post and topic:** choose Submit, then Post. Enter a valid title and content. In Topics, type a valid name and press Enter; confirm it appears as a chip before submitting. A new valid topic is created when the post submission succeeds, not merely when text is entered. The current validator accepts 3–24 letters; check the current rule if input is rejected. Success navigates to `/post/:id`.
6. **Comment on a post or reply:** on a post detail page, choose Comment to open the inline composer, enter the message, and submit. Confirm the response count changes and the comment appears. Use a comment's Reply action to create a nested reply; don't confuse this with creating a top-level thread. Detail loads increment visit counters, so avoid repeated loads of existing content when counters matter.
7. **Create and discuss a thread:** choose Submit, then Thread. A top-level thread uses a content field and topic chip, without a post title. After submission, verify `/thread/:id`; use Reply for a reply or Quote for a quoted response, then confirm it appears in the thread chain.
8. **Use the inbox:** open Inbox and choose Context to navigate to the notification's related post, comment, thread, profile, or appeal. Dismiss marks a notification viewed; opening Inbox alone does not. Use per-item Dismiss for a single fixture and reserve Dismiss All for an explicitly authorized test.
9. **Change personal filters:** open the profile link, choose Profile, then Filters. Select Show, Mask, or Filter for NSFW/spoiler content and use Save; Cancel reloads saved preferences. The page lists muted and blocked users/topics. Mute hides content from feeds/search without preventing interactions. Block also restricts interactions and removes existing follows; unblocking does not restore them. Use disposable accounts/topics for block tests.
10. **Use content actions:** on a post or thread, use the header's positive, misleading, or negative vote controls separately from the ellipsis Options menu; some vote types may be disabled. Before testing votes, record the user's active vote and displayed counts. Clicking the active category removes that vote; choosing another category moves the vote rather than adding a second one. Wait for the settled counts and restore the initial vote. Share requests copying the current page URL to the clipboard and shows a success hint without navigating; verify by pasting when clipboard behavior matters, since the hint alone does not confirm the browser accepted the copy. The menu may offer Save, Report, Edit, Archive/Delete, or moderation actions depending on ownership, role, content type, and status. Save toggles to Unsave after success; reread the page before interpreting the menu or save count, and restore the initial state when testing this reversible action. Archive toggles active/archived state and offers Unarchive for archived content; verify the marker, message, and restored status using isolated content. Delete opens a Confirm Deletion prompt; after confirmation, the post redirects to `/feed/search`. Verify the record is unavailable by ID rather than relying only on the success toast, and use isolated content. Lock/Unlock toggles item state but creates moderator audit entries that remain after restoration. Slow Mode applies the selected allowed interval to a post, thread, or gallery; verify the visible interval marker, then clear it. Setting and clearing it also leaves moderator audit entries. App Pin creates a persistent pin and has no inverse in this menu, so don't apply it to reusable content unless the pinned state is intended to remain. Confirm the target and any prompt first. Awards spend 256 tokens and notify another user, so only test them with explicit scope and suitable sample accounts.
11. **Use role tools:** follow a visible Moderator, Admin, or Developer navbar link to the corresponding tools. These links are role-gated, and topic moderation can also depend on assignment. Do not treat a hidden link or client-side abort alone as proof of server-side authorization; verify the backend contract when access control is in scope.
12. **Update profile and preferences:** `/settings/profile` edits username, link, and Markdown description; email is read-only. Update saves, and Cancel reloads the profile. `/settings/preferences` saves or reloads hover-animation and hint-duration choices, in-app/email notifications, and profile audience (`public`, `members`, or `private`). Check audience changes from an appropriately signed-out or separate member session.
13. **Manage account security:** `/settings/misc` can request an account-confirmation email, request a password-reset link, or sign out all other sessions while keeping the current session active. Complete password reset from the emailed `/settings/reset-password?id=...` link; it requires the account email and matching new-password fields and invalidates existing sessions. Confirmation emails currently link to `/profile?confirmation=...`, but the profile middleware checks `from.query` instead of the incoming `to.query`; treat direct confirmation as a suspected defect and verify the confirmed state before calling it successful.
14. **Delete an account:** `/settings/delete` exists but is not linked from the current settings tab list. The page requires the current password and exact username, then offers permanent deletion while keeping published content attributed to “deleted”, or deletion of eligible content with discussion-dependent redaction. Historical votes remain. Do not exercise either option without explicit destructive-test authorization and an isolated account/database.
15. **Save a post draft:** in Submit > Post, enter a valid title and choose Save or Update; Ctrl+S/Cmd+S also saves. Open Drafts to load or delete a saved post/reply draft. Draft deletion is immediate, so use a uniquely named fixture and verify it is gone. If deletion returns an authorization error, confirm the draft remains and inspect its Developer error entry; do not bypass the route or claim cleanup succeeded. Drafts are currently implemented in the Post editor, not every editor tab.
16. **Publish a Link:** in Submit > Link, enter an HTTP(S) URL. The preview may fill an empty title/description from page metadata; review and edit these fields, select at least one topic, and submit. Confirm the resulting `/link/:id` page and destination before following external links.
17. **Publish an image gallery:** in Submit > Image, choose Browse, select an image, and complete the uploader before publishing. Add a title (4–128 characters), optional description (up to 256 characters), tags, and at least one topic; submit and verify the Gallery feed result. Uploads create media before gallery publication, so use a known-good fixture and remove only that fixture through the UI when cleanup is authorized.
18. **Send feedback:** authenticated users can open the navbar Feedback control; `/contact` shows the feedback form whenever feedback is enabled. Submission requires an authenticated session unless anonymous feedback is enabled in site settings. Feedback must be nonempty. Submissions are limited to five per minute per resolved client IP, so avoid repeated attempts when checking rate limits. Admins can review items in Admin > Feedback, refresh, show dismissed items, and dismiss an active item.
19. **Report content and appeal a removal:** use Report from a content action menu or a comment action. The form warns that the report goes to moderators; blank submission shows "Enter a reason for this report." and keeps the form open, while Cancel closes without submitting. Enter a nonblank reason and submit; authentication is required and later complaints may append to the existing report for that subject. For a removed subject, open its report notification in Inbox using Context (Appeal), provide an appeal reason of at least three characters, and confirm the displayed pending/accepted/rejected state. Only removed reports without a previous appeal can be appealed.
20. **Review reports (Moderator):** open Moderator > Reports or a topic's Tools > Reports. Filter by topic when offered, select a report stage, inspect complaint reasons/history, and view the subject before acting. Close, remove, remove a topic association, reopen, and accept/reject an appeal have different role/status requirements; each decision requires a reason. Use isolated reports because these actions alter content or moderation history. Audio, Video, and Poll editor tabs are not publishable workflows; use them only to check their unavailable state.

### Configure Site Settings (Admin)

1. Sign in with an admin account, open Admin from the navbar, then choose Settings. The Admin parent route may reopen its remembered tab; use the Settings tab to reach `/admin/settings`.
2. Select a section from the settings panel. The page edits a local draft: Save submits the complete application-settings object and refreshes the app-wide settings; Cancel reloads the last saved values. Do not save while merely inspecting, and verify a changed setting with the affected user workflow after saving.
3. Use **feeds** to show or hide Search, Topics, and Home. Use **discussion** to enable Posts, Threads, Links, or Polls and their separate feeds. Disabling a content type can also turn off its feed. Poll publishing is marked unfinished.
4. Use **topics** to set the 1–5 topic submission limit, per-topic moderator request capacity, approval threshold, and optional established-topic allowlist. Enabling topic restriction can populate the allowlist from currently available topics; review the resulting list before saving. Use **moderation** to configure allowed slow-mode intervals in seconds.
5. Use **voting** to enable voting and the misleading/negative options. Use **content** to choose Show, Mask, or Hide for NSFW and spoiler content.
6. Use **media** to configure image uploads, size limit, post/thread attachments, gallery publishing/feed, and audio/video switches. Token support is reserved; audio and video publishing are marked unfinished, so do not treat their controls as evidence of supported end-to-end workflows.
7. Use **email** for public support/additional contact addresses and email-spool limits, **feedback** to enable feedback and optionally allow anonymous submissions, and **about** to edit the Markdown summary shown on `/about`. Email addresses and spool limits do not configure SMTP delivery.
8. Treat saving a moderation approval-threshold change as a workflow mutation: the update re-evaluates pending moderator requests and can grant moderator roles/topic assignments, close requests, and send notifications. Use a disposable deployment when validating that behavior.

Admin Settings are shared application data persisted through `POST /api/admin/settings/:id/update`; they are not per-user preferences. Deployment settings such as `PORT`, `NUXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, `NUXT_TRUSTED_PROXIES`, `NUXT_DATA_PATH`, SurrealDB connection mode/URL, and SMTP host/credentials belong in the deployment `.env`. Environment changes take effect after restarting the app process, not by saving this page; never inspect, print, or change production secrets during browser validation.

For a dedicated sample deployment, representative fixtures may be left in place when the owner requests that; keep them clearly recognizable and isolated from production. Otherwise, use unique fixtures and follow the cleanup guidance below.

## 3. Inspect the Browser

Before any browser inspection or interaction, get explicit permission unless the user explicitly requested browser validation. This includes snapshots, screenshots, DOM or console inspection, page scripts, navigation, clicks, scrolling, and resizing. A shared, visible, or active tab is not permission. If permission is absent, ask first and continue with non-browser checks where possible.

1. Reuse the shared page when available; do not open a duplicate tab without a reason.
2. Take a snapshot first. Note the full URL, app instance/environment, signed-in account, controls, and visible errors. Re-read the page at the start of each new interaction sequence; a shared tab may have changed since the previous turn. After navigation, take a fresh snapshot before reusing element references.
3. On an authenticated ClassicForum page, right-click the navbar profile link to open UserManager and inspect locally saved profiles. Use it to switch among sessions already authenticated in this browser; `New Login` opens the normal login flow. Do not use the adjacent remove action unless intentionally invalidating that saved session.
4. Use accessible snapshot references for clicks. Treat references as current-page state: refresh the snapshot after navigation or a substantial UI change instead of reusing stale references. Use screenshots for layout and snapshots for controls and their state.
5. Go straight to affected routes when that is clearer than navigating unrelated UI. Distinguish an in-app link transition from a direct URL load or reload; a successful SPA transition does not verify SSR or hard-refresh behavior. For suspected redirects, record the requested URL, response status and `Location` when available, and final browser URL.
6. If a framework-driven target cannot be activated from the snapshot, use a stable selector with the Playwright `page` API. For text entry, prefer accessible role or placeholder locators, fill the field, and verify its value and resulting UI state. Do not access `document` or `window` directly through the Playwright tool when its provided `page` API is required.
7. Use Playwright only when the browser's page, navigation, click, typing, or dialog tools cannot do the check. Keep each Playwright snippet focused on one interaction and verify the resulting URL and a fresh snapshot afterward.
8. Check `/api/health` before interpreting widespread `503` responses. If the app or database is not ready, stop feature checks until startup completes.

### Reliable Interaction Loop

1. Start each journey with `read_page`; confirm the full URL, app environment, signed-in account, and target control.
2. Prefer visible links and tabs for in-app workflow navigation. Use `navigate_page` for direct-entry, refresh, back, or forward checks. After navigation or a substantial UI change, call `read_page` and reacquire references before acting again.
3. Enter text using a current accessible textbox reference; reread the page and verify its value and validation state before submitting. If reference-based entry times out while the field is visible, take a fresh snapshot and use an accessible Playwright locator instead of retrying a stale reference. Submit once, then wait for the pending/spinner state to settle.
4. Verify success with a user-visible confirmation and the resulting route or persisted list/detail state. Modal closure or a changed button alone does not prove a mutation succeeded.
5. On `502`/`503` or another transport error, stop retries; check `/api/health`, the newest Developer > Errors entry, and the target record/list to determine whether the mutation landed. Retry only after the app/database are ready and the target record is confirmed absent.
6. On `401`/`403`, confirm the signed-in identity and expected ownership/role, inspect the matching error, and verify the target remains unchanged. Do not retry by bypassing the UI/API authorization path. If a `pageerror` occurs, reread the page; continue only if the intended controls are usable, and record the error separately from the workflow result.

## 4. Exercise Flows Safely

1. Check route load, main content, controls, and expected empty, error, or success states.
2. Start with read-only actions. Use one-time test data that is uniquely identifiable and can be cleaned up, or legitimate reusable fixtures with realistic, stable content. In a development environment, existing content may be used for mutations when the user explicitly approves it; record its initial state and restore reversible changes after the test. Approval applies only to the described workflow and does not authorize unrelated deletion, publishing, session revocation, or account changes.
3. Before submitting a form, inspect its visible validation state and required fields. If a value is rejected, check the field's validation rule or visible hint instead of trying arbitrary variants. Confirm autocomplete or chip inputs are actually accepted before submitting.
4. After a successful mutation, record its generated ID and destination, then verify the destination with a direct URL load or reload when route handling is under test. Inspect the current state before cleanup so only the test fixture is affected.
5. Account for read-like actions that mutate data. Opening a detail page may increment a visit/view counter; avoid repeated requests to existing content when that side effect matters, and note that deleting a test item may not undo counters or other derived history.
6. For confirmations, verify the prompt. Dismiss it if the destructive action is outside scope.
7. Record the route, action, expected and observed results, and relevant browser console or request errors.
8. Separate application regressions from environment or data problems, such as unavailable APIs, missing media, or stale records. For legacy metadata that points to files lost during a restore or reformat, compare against a known-good asset uploaded during this pass. Recheck after navigation before attributing old console events to a route.

## Troubleshooting

1. For API failures, inspect the newest developer error entry: timestamp, stack, method, and request path. Compare timestamps after retries; older errors remain in the list.
2. For runtime type errors, trace the value from the route through the database/shared boundary. Do not assume a JSON-looking ID is a string; inspect the SDK value and preserve the declared contract. Prefer a focused browser reproduction over a broad database rewrite.
3. For media issues, upload a known-good repository asset. Verify the CDN URL loads and inspect the image's `complete`, `naturalWidth`, and `naturalHeight`; compare its bare ID with the stored filename if needed. A legacy 404 alone does not prove an upload regression.
4. Clean up test mutations through the UI when possible. For a private image, verify the owner's delete/refund result and that scheduled cleanup removes its file. For a test reply, open its detail page, delete it through its options menu, and confirm it disappears. Do not overwrite or discard existing drafts or user data to make a test pass.

## 5. Report Coverage

1. List the app instance/version, account state, journeys checked, and outcomes. For route issues, distinguish in-app navigation from direct load/reload and include the requested and final URLs plus status/redirect evidence.
2. Separate failures from blocked or untested flows. Say which dependency or safety limit prevented a check.
3. Call out non-browser behavior that still needs focused tests, database checks, or operational validation.
4. Do not claim a full pass when infrastructure failed or requirements remain untested.
